text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 use runs above peers in every complexity band with the steepest excess in sicker patients, but documentation is too thin to say whether the high-level visits are supported.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 billing is concentrated where it would be most expected, among patients with 4 or more conditions (e.g., C0010436, C0011388), and only a small share falls on low-complexity patients, which leans toward a sicker panel. Even so, the provider bills 99215 at roughly double the all-provider rate within each band from 1 to 5+ conditions, so complexity alone does not fully explain the pattern, and the sampled low-complexity 99215s (e.g., C0010444, C0011100, C0011574 with no chronic conditions) deserve scrutiny. Records came back for only a tiny fraction of claims with a single documented 99215 (C0011079, supported at high MDM), so the absence of unsupported claims says little either way, and the few notes claiming moderate-plus data reviewed without a lab line are weak signals, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts targeted at the low-complexity 99215 claims and a larger sample of 4+ condition 99215s to test whether documented MDM supports the billed level, checking for cloned or templated notes."}
